instructions: Add one confirmed row per concrete evidence item. Cite canonical source files, copy verifier excerpts verbatim, and judge source presence separately from recovery.

criteria.criterion: Access legislation.gov.uk and reach Data Protection Act 2018 in Original (As enacted) Introductory Text (or clearly report blocker)
criteria.description: Agent navigates to the Data Protection Act 2018 on legislation.gov.uk, switches to the “Original (As enacted)” version, and opens “Introductory Text”. Full credit if the agent either (a) successfully reaches the as-enacted Introductory Text, or (b) makes a reasonable attempt but is prevented by an external issue (CAPTCHA, outage, access denied, infinite loading) and clearly reports the blocker and where it occurred. Partial credit if the agent reaches the Act but does not clearly confirm as-enacted vs revised, or cannot reach Introductory Text but still demonstrates it is using the as-enacted view elsewhere on the site.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Action History shows navigation to https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2018/12/introduction/enacted from the as-enacted contents page. Screenshot 3 (latest confirming version selector) shows breadcrumb ending “Introduction” and the “Original (As enacted)” option selected with status “This is the original version (as it was originally enacted).” Screenshot 4 shows the Introductory Text content (chapter line/long title/date) but does not itself display the version selector.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: The agent demonstrably reached the Introduction/Introductory Text content, and there is clear evidence (Screenshot 3 + the /enacted URL in action history) that the session is in the Original (As enacted) version. This satisfies the navigation requirement.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows a legislation.gov.uk page displaying the heading “Data Protection Act 2018” with the line “2018 CHAPTER 12” beneath it. Below that is the long-title paragraph beginning “An Act to make provision for the regulation of the processing of information relating to individuals; …” and at the end of that block the date in brackets “[23rd May 2018]”. The left panel shows “Advanced Features” and navigation items like “Opening Options” and “More Resources.” A “Next: Provision” button is visible, which is consistent with being in the Introductory Text section.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The screenshot evidences the Act’s Introductory Text content (title, chapter line, long title, and Royal Assent date). However, nothing in the visible area explicitly indicates the version is “Original (As enacted)” (e.g., no visible “Original/Latest available” selector or “as enacted” label in the UI). So the screenshot supports reaching Introductory Text for the Act, but does not conclusively confirm the as-enacted view from pixels alone.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent claims it is the Original (As enacted) version; the screenshot shows Introductory Text content but does not visibly show an “Original (As enacted)” indicator. No blocker is shown.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows the legislation.gov.uk page for “Data Protection Act 2018” with breadcrumb “UK Public General Acts > 2018 c. 12 > Introduction”. In the left “What Version” box, “Original (As enacted)” is selected (checked) and the main panel shows a “Status: This is the original version (as it was originally enacted).” message. The page has navigation buttons including “Next: Provision”. The visible content is the Introduction page header area; the actual Introductory Text contents (chapter number line, long title, Royal Assent date) are not visible in the screenshot.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The screenshot supports that the agent reached the Data Protection Act 2018 and is on the “Introduction” page in “Original (As enacted)” view, satisfying the navigation/state portion of the criterion. However, the screenshot does not display the Introductory Text details (chapter number/long title/Royal Assent date) to verify those values from the image alone.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent’s predicted output includes chapter number, long title, and Royal Assent date, but none of those specific items are visible in this screenshot; only the as-enacted status and that the page is “Introduction” are visible.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows the legislation.gov.uk page for “Data Protection Act 2018” with the “Table of Contents” tab selected. In the left sidebar under “What Version”, “Original (As enacted)” is selected (check mark next to it). In the main contents list, “Introductory Text” is visible as a heading, and below it “PART 1 Preliminary” appears. A status box reads: “Status: This is the original version (as it was originally enacted).”
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The screenshot supports that the agent is on the Data Protection Act 2018 and is using the Original (As enacted) version, and that the Introductory Text section is present/visible in the table of contents. However, it does not show the Introductory Text page content itself (e.g., the long title and Royal Assent date text are not visible in this screenshot), only the ToC entry/heading. This is still strong evidence of reaching the as-enacted context with Introductory Text available.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent action history/predicted output implies they opened the Introductory Text page to extract chapter number/long title/Royal Assent date; this screenshot instead shows the table of contents view with “Introductory Text” listed, not the detailed Introductory Text content where those details would appear.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows legislation.gov.uk on the “Data Protection Act 2018” page with the “Table of Contents” tab selected. In the left “What Version” panel, “Latest available (Revised)” appears selected (dark/checked), and “Original (As enacted)” is visible as an unselected option below. A green “Changes to legislation” box states the Act is “up to date with all changes known to be in force on or before 11 September 2026.” There is a link “Introductory Text” visible below the contents area, but the screenshot does not show the Introductory Text page itself, nor any chapter number, long title text, or Royal Assent date.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: This screenshot does not confirm the agent reached the Original (As enacted) Introductory Text. It instead shows the Table of Contents view with the revised/latest version selected and a “Changes to legislation” notice consistent with a revised view. Since Introductory Text content is not open and the as-enacted selection is not shown as active, the criterion is not satisfied based on the visible evidence.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Action history/predicted output indicate the agent switched to “Original (As enacted)” and opened Introductory Text, but the screenshot shows “Latest available (Revised)” selected and still on the Table of Contents tab, not the Introductory Text page. The predicted output’s chapter number/long title/Royal Assent date are not visible anywhere in the screenshot.

Partial credit if the chapter number is correct but formatting differs slightly. If the agent is blocked from viewing the as-enacted Introductory Text after a reasonable attempt (as documented in the navigation criterion), award partial credit if it explicitly states it cannot verify the chapter number due to access issues (no guessing); no credit if it fabricates a value without support.

criteria.criterion: Count top-level Parts in as-enacted table of contents (Parts only, exclude nested Parts in Schedules)
criteria.description: Report the number of top-level Parts shown in the as-enacted table of contents, counting only the Act’s top-level Parts and excluding any Parts within Schedules. Full credit if the count matches the as-enacted contents (expected 7). Partial credit if the agent attempts counting from the as-enacted contents but makes a small counting error or does not clearly indicate it excluded nested Schedule Parts. If blocked from accessing the as-enacted table of contents after a reasonable attempt, award partial credit if the agent states it cannot verify the count due to access issues (no guessing).

screenshot_context.verifier_justification: Although the agent’s answer of 7 Parts is plausibly correct for this Act, the provided visual evidence does not substantiate that the agent actually verified/counts all top-level Parts from the as-enacted ToC. Award partial credit for giving the correct number but without evidentiary support in the screenshots.

evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Predicted output reports “Number of top-level Parts…: 7”, but the screenshot only visibly shows “PART 1 Preliminary” and not the full list of Parts needed to substantiate the count.
